title: A Alibi for the Inheritance
premise: Insurance investigator Juniper Vane receives a confession letter for the death of matriarch Cordelia Ashcombe—postmarked the day after her funeral and signed by Juniper's long-vanished mother, who once worked as the Ashcombes' housekeeper. Returning to the decaying estate of Hollowmere to prove or destroy the letter's claims, Juniper uncovers a forged will, a family that thrives on curated silence, and evidence that Cordelia's death was staged to protect someone she loved. As the estate's heirs close ranks and the statute on the insurance payout expires in thirty days, Juniper must choose between exposing the truth that would ruin an innocent person and burying it to honor their mother's final act of loyalty. In the end, Juniper discovers Cordelia orchestrated her own death's ambiguity as a gift—and delivers a verdict that closes the case without breaking it open.
about_author: Silas Eastwick is a former probate clerk from coastal Maine who spent eleven years cataloguing disputed estates before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about families whose secrets outlive them, drawing on real case files he was never allowed to discuss.

chapters.title: The Postmark
chapters.summary: Juniper Vane, meticulous and emotionally walled-off, opens a confession letter signed by their estranged mother, postmarked one day after Cordelia Ashcombe's funeral. The handwriting is unmistakable. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: cold dread cracking into old grief.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Rising
chapters.summary: Juniper travels to the crumbling Ashcombe estate, posing as an insurance adjuster reviewing the large policy on Cordelia's life. The house smells of lilies and denial. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: wary return to a world they escaped.

chapters.title: The Grieving Heirs
chapters.summary: Juniper meets the three heirs: eldest son Ambrose, brittle daughter-in-law Marguerite, and grandson Toby, who seems genuinely shattered. Each performs grief differently. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: reading people like documents, finding every page altered.

chapters.title: A Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Juniper watches their mother, Ruth, pack in the night after leaving service at Hollowmere, refusing to explain. POV: alternating Juniper present/Ruth past. Emotional beat: the wound the letter has reopened.

chapters.title: The Closed File
chapters.summary: The coroner ruled Cordelia's death—fall down the cellar stairs—an accident. Juniper pulls the file and finds the scene photos oddly sparse, as if curated. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: professional instinct sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ambrose shows Juniper the estate's debts; Hollowmere is drowning, and the insurance payout is its only lifeline. His desperation wears a gentleman's mask. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: identifying motive number one.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Garden
chapters.summary: Marguerite, tending roses her mother-in-law forbade, lets slip that Cordelia changed her will weeks before dying—but the new will has vanished. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: complicity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Toby's Testimony
chapters.summary: Toby, Cordelia's favorite, recalls his grandmother burning papers in her study the last week of her life, humming. He thought nothing of it then. POV: Toby. Emotional beat: innocence beginning to doubt itself.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Room
chapters.summary: Juniper searches the preserved servants' quarters and finds scratch marks inside Ruth's old wardrobe—tally marks, or letters. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: touching the ghost of a mother who planned something.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Juniper confirms the insurer will pay out automatically unless fraud is proven within thirty days. The clock becomes a character. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: pressure transforming curiosity into urgency.

chapters.title: The Village Remembers
chapters.summary: In town, the pub landlady reveals Ruth left Hollowmere abruptly twenty-five years ago, pregnant, after 'something with the mistress.' No one will say what. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the past pressing against the present.

chapters.title: Cellar Light
chapters.summary: Juniper examines the cellar stairs where Cordelia fell and notices the handrail was freshly oiled—someone maintained it after the death. Why? POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: first hard evidence of staging.

chapters.title: Ambrose Threatens
chapters.summary: Ambrose warns Juniper off, invoking the insurer's deadline and hinting at Ruth's 'history of instability.' POV: Ambrose. Emotional beat: menace dressed as concern.

chapters.title: The Confession Reread
chapters.summary: Juniper studies the letter under magnification: the ink is old, but the paper isn't. Someone aged a genuine document—or assembled one. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: doubt turning inward, toward their own mother.

chapters.title: Ruth's Letters
chapters.summary: In a storage unit Ruth rented before vanishing, Juniper finds unsent letters to Cordelia spanning decades—a secret correspondence between mistress and maid. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: discovering a relationship no one knew existed.

chapters.title: What Cordelia Knew
chapters.summary: The letters reveal Cordelia covered up a fatal accident years ago—one involving the heirs' father—to protect the family name. Ruth helped bury it. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the ground shifting beneath every assumption.

chapters.title: Marguerite Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted gently, Marguerite admits she saw Ambrose near the cellar that night but swore silence because he paid her father's debts. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: guilt finally outweighing survival.

chapters.title: The Vanished Will
chapters.summary: Juniper traces the missing will to the family solicitor, who confesses Ambrose pressured him to suppress it—it cut Ambrose out almost entirely. POV: solicitor (via Juniper's interview). Emotional beat: motive crystallizing.

chapters.title: Toby Follows
chapters.summary: Toby, having shadowed Juniper, reveals he found his grandmother's diary hidden in the conservatory organ. He hasn't read it. He hands it over trembling. POV: Toby. Emotional beat: loyalty choosing truth.

chapters.title: The Diary
chapters.summary: Cordelia's diary describes a diagnosis—terminal, hidden—and a plan she calls 'the arrangement,' written in deliberately vague terms. She knew she was dying. POV: excerpts through Juniper. Emotional beat: awe and unease entwined.

chapters.title: Night Visitor
chapters.summary: Someone searches Juniper's room at the inn. Nothing is taken except a photocopy of the confession letter. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the case now watching back.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Alibi
chapters.summary: Ambrose produces witnesses placing him at a charity dinner the night of the fall—the alibi is airtight, too airtight, arranged in advance. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: realizing the alibi itself is the tell.

chapters.title: A Alibi for the Inheritance
chapters.summary: Juniper reconstructs it: Cordelia built Ambrose's alibi herself, scheduling the dinner, so suspicion would never touch him. She was protecting him from himself. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the title's meaning landing like a blow.

chapters.title: Ruth Returns
chapters.summary: Following a lead from the letters, Juniper finds Ruth alive in a coastal hospice, dying, lucid. She sent the confession to force Juniper home before it was too late to choose. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: reunion as excavation.

chapters.title: Mother's Truth
chapters.summary: Ruth confesses: Cordelia asked her to help stage an ambiguous death—neither suicide nor murder provable—so the insurance would pay and Ambrose would be saved from ruin and prosecution both. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: love and deception indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Why Juniper
chapters.summary: Ruth admits she stayed away for twenty-five years because Cordelia paid for Juniper's education anonymously—her silence was the price. Juniper was bought and never knew. POV: Ruth/Juniper. Emotional beat: fury and heartbreak colliding.

chapters.title: The Oiled Rail
chapters.summary: Juniper realizes Ruth oiled the rail afterward—not to hide guilt, but because Cordelia's grip had weakened; she'd nearly fallen twice before. It was mercy maintenance. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: evidence reframed as tenderness.

chapters.title: Ambrose Suspects
chapters.summary: Ambrose learns Juniper met Ruth and panics, threatening exposure of Ruth as a confessed killer. His fear reveals he suspects the truth and cannot bear it. POV: Ambrose. Emotional beat: a man cornered by his own inheritance.

chapters.title: Deadline Eve
chapters.summary: Day twenty-nine. Juniper holds everything needed to void the claim and brand Ruth a murderer—or let a staged death stand. Neither choice is clean. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the investigator's creed breaking apart.

chapters.title: The Study Fire
chapters.summary: Reenacting Cordelia's last night from the diary, Juniper understands: Cordelia chose the stairs herself, timed to the dinner, leaving the diary where Toby would someday find it. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: seeing the dead woman's design whole.

chapters.title: Climax: The Reading
chapters.summary: Juniper gathers the heirs and reads Cordelia's diary aloud, revealing the terminal diagnosis, the arrangement, and the vanished will—which named Toby principal heir, with Ambrose provided for by the insurance. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Ambrose Unmade
chapters.summary: Ambrose collapses—not from exposure but relief; he'd half-known and spent his life paying for a crime never committed. He signs away contest of the will. POV: Ambrose. Emotional beat: guilt dissolving into grief.

chapters.title: The Insurer's Verdict
chapters.summary: Juniper files a report declaring the death accidental, closing the claim. Their photographic memory holds every contradiction—and they choose which ones to keep. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: complicity chosen knowingly.

chapters.title: Ruth's Last Day
chapters.summary: Juniper sits with Ruth, who asks only whether Cordelia's plan held. Juniper tells her it did. Ruth dies at peace, still keeping some secrets. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: forgiveness without absolution.

chapters.title: What Juniper Keeps
chapters.summary: Juniper burns the confession letter and the tally-marked wardrobe panel, preserving the diary alone as record. Some truths are load-bearing; remove them and the house falls. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: becoming keeper of the arrangement.

chapters.title: Toby's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Toby takes ownership of Hollowmere, promising Marguerite a home for life. He asks Juniper what really happened; Juniper says the stairs were oiled out of love. Both understand. POV: Toby. Emotional beat: the next generation inheriting mercy.

chapters.title: The Empty File
chapters.summary: Back at the office, Juniper closes the Ashcombe file—the first case they've ever closed with a lie inside it. The blank space where the truth should be feels less like failure than authorship. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: identity remade.

chapters.title: Postmark Returned
chapters.summary: Juniper mails a letter to the hospice address, knowing no one will collect it: a full account of what they found and chose, written for no one and everyone. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: mourning made procedural, therefore bearable.

chapters.title: Coda: Hollowmere in Spring
chapters.summary: Months later, Juniper visits the estate, roses blooming where Marguerite planted them against Cordelia's rules. On the cellar door, fresh oil gleams. Some cases are never closed—only carried. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
